summary: Resumed the existing draft branch (bootstrap-only, zero changed files at resume) and completed LC-AUD-001's full handoff in priority order, then isolated shared curriculum infrastructure within this task's declared write scopes. Resolved all three cross-level capability-id collisions (F1: B1's report_a_problem renamed to escalate_and_resolve_a_problem, distinct from A2's identically-named capability; F2: C1's infer_implied_meaning renamed to infer_implied_meaning_in_unfamiliar_context, escalating B2's should-scope receptive capability; F3: C2's reformulate_for_a_different_audience renamed to reformulate_dense_source_for_a_new_audience, ending the collision with C1's identically-named capability and correcting C2's factually-contradicted 'first mediation task' claim). Applied all nineteen cross-level prerequisite-string fixes (F4, F5, F6) at high/medium confidence, deliberately leaving the one low-confidence C2 mapping (sustain_coherence_across_topic_shifts) unresolved with an explicit unresolvedPrerequisiteNote for human curriculum-design judgment, per the audit's own instruction not to auto-apply it. Added a prerequisiteRisk bridging note to B1's sustain_topic_change since its real A2 prerequisite is should-scope, not guaranteed (F4b). Added CEFR Companion Volume references to all 19 A2 capabilities, the only level with zero coverage (F7). Reconciled B1's problem/B2's problem_type/C1's proposed negotiated_item into one documented type family (F9, docs/curriculum/semantic-types.md) rather than three overlapping types. Fixed both pattern-id reuse hazards (F10: B1's because_reason_pattern marked as A2 reuse, not a second introduction; F11: C2's academic hedging form renamed to academic_hedging_pattern rather than reusing B2's colloquial hedging_pattern id). Consolidated B2's and C1's duplicate CORE evaluator asks into one register-appropriateness dimension and one discourse-coherence-scoring path (F8, docs/curriculum/core-engine-requirements.md), and added the shared contract shape (registerAppropriateness/discourseCoherence fields, both checked:false by default) to responseEvaluation.js's base() result — zero behavioural change for any live Pre-A1/A1 capability, confirmed by full check:all and targeted evaluator-check reruns. Isolated shared curriculum infrastructure: added curriculum/levelMaps.js, a small additive registry every level's own capability-to-intent map registers itself in, replacing scaffolding.js's previous direct import of only Pre-A1's map — which was a real, live bug (any lookup for one of A1's own intents silently returned null, disabling novelty-based support scaling for A1's original intents, not just failing loudly). Added scripts/check-cross-level-ids.mjs (wired into check:all) as the mechanical guard that fails the build the moment two registered levels declare the same bare capability id, directly automating the collision class LC-AUD-001 had to find by hand. A full architecture survey found five more shared, flat, level-unaware surfaces (evaluator-dispatch switch, SessionRunner/formatChoice/miniStory tables, session.js's item/error/canDo tables, semanticContext.js's five registries, learnerModel.js's FACT_TYPES/MILESTONE_LEVELS, readiness.js/graduation.js's Pre-A1-only scoping, i18n's 8-file flat structure) — each deliberately left unrefactored and recorded with reasoning in docs/curriculum/curriculum-isolation-plan.md, since none has a real second-level runtime consumer yet to validate a registry-style split against; building that extension mechanism now, before any A2+ content exists, would be speculative rather than informed, and several are large live surfaces powering the shipped Pre-A1/A1 experience where an unvalidated refactor is a real regression risk. No blueprint file lost data, no runtime module was made to import design-artifact blueprints, A1 stays available:false, Pre-A1 stays frozen and untouched, no Supabase/voice/provider-policy surface was touched.
